analyticalQuestion: Can a signed or separable bilinear parabolic time packet retain entry-direction information without paying either inverse-height K squared sampling or temporal Gram density?
takeaway: A nonzero-mean packet retains constant directional data only with an inverse-height K squared diagonal cost, dense same-direction packets have a growing finite Gram constant, the exact adjoint heat packet has the same scaling, and an even-touch signed precursor or zero-mean factor has zero response.
nonColorEncoding: solid, dashed, dash-dot, and dotted lines
circle, square, triangle, cross, and diamond markers

panels.A: nonzero-mean box packet: critical K squared cost versus strong-ledger constant
panels.B: same-direction finite box Gram largest eigenvalue with exact lower and upper bounds
panels.C: adjoint heat packet: H-minus-one-normalized K squared cost versus strong-ledger constant
panels.D: even-touch positive, Jordan, signed, and zero-mean responses

claimBoundary: Panels A-C are exact finite packet or linear heat models. Panel D is a forced-parabolic even touch and is not an NSE trajectory. For the separately certified covariant family a_K=a0*K, the genuine R0.71O/R0.71P NSE information is limited to the initial observation face: A_plus=a0^2*K^2/4, K^-2*A_plus=a0^2/4, and the bare Leray time-integral scale K^-2. It is not plotted as a positive-time result. No temporal packing, continuation, singularity, regularity, originality, or Millennium-problem claim is shown.
